hypotheses.title: Rain lowers Election-Day turnout
hypotheses.claim: Each inch of rain cuts turnout by about one percentage point (Gomez, Hansford & Krause 2007, Journal of Politics).
hypotheses.design: All counties with votes counted. Turnout surprise (live expected vote vs. pre-election expectation, in points) regressed on today's precipitation, with state fixed effects, standard errors clustered by state.
hypotheses.reading: Needs more counties reporting (0 with votes, 0 with at least 1 mm of rain).

hypotheses.title: Easy mail and early voting blunt the rain effect
hypotheses.claim: Where most votes are cast before Election Day, a rainy Tuesday matters less (the convenience-voting argument: Gronke et al. 2008; Gomez, Hansford & Krause 2007 on absentee states; Thompson, Wu, Yoder & Hall 2020 on vote-by-mail).
hypotheses.design: Counties within 100 km of a state line where the mail rule changes (no-excuse or all-mail on one side, excuse-required on the other). Turnout surprise regressed on which side of the line the county is on, distance to the line (separately on each side), rain, and side x rain, with a fixed effect for each state pair; standard errors clustered by state pair. The side x rain term is the test: a negative number means rain costs more turnout on the restrictive side of the same storm.
hypotheses.reading: Border sample so far: 0 counties with votes within 100 km of a rules line, 0 of them wet. Needs about 60 and 15.

hypotheses.title: Rain helps Republicans
hypotheses.claim: Rain shifts the vote toward Republicans because the voters it keeps home lean Democratic (Gomez, Hansford & Krause 2007); the newer argument is that the effect shrinks or reverses where Democrats vote by mail.
hypotheses.design: Counties with votes counted. The county's Democratic two-way share in the House race tonight minus Harris's 2024 two-way share, regressed on rain and rain x convenience-voting state, with state fixed effects; errors clustered by state. A negative rain coefficient means rain is moving the count toward Republicans in excuse-required states.
hypotheses.reading: Needs about 150 counties with both parties' votes counted (0 so far).
